label: payment-threshold-must-be-the-quoted-amount
reasoning: Fixed a rejection waiting to happen at the payment step, before it ever fired. The preview email quotes an exact SOL figure, and both the shop page and the email promise that anything within 5% of it counts as paid. Step 7 of the fulfillment runbook, though, only said to verify against 'required_lamports x 0.95' without saying which required amount, and nothing in code or tests pinned it - the threshold is passed in by hand on each run. A run that reads that line and computes $15 at today's SOL price instead of reading the quote off the pending entry rejects a customer who paid exactly what they were told to pay, any time SOL fell more than 5% between the preview and the payment. That is not a remote scenario: the one pending preview was quoted at 7397 cents per SOL and SOL is 7253 today, so 1.9% of the 5% margin is already spent after a week, against a 14-day expiry window. The failure would also have been near-invisible - the customer gets a polite 'we couldn't verify that' email and almost certainly walks, and the run recording it has no reason to suspect its own threshold. Same shape as the four findings before it this week: a promise made in one place and the machinery behind it built in another, the path between never walked - only this one sits on the last step before revenue, where everything upstream can work and still convert nothing. Fix: runbook step 7 now names the source explicitly - the threshold comes from expected_lamports stored on the pending entry (the figure actually quoted), never recomputed at the current price - and the rule is executable rather than prose via ops.solpay.min_accepted_lamports(), with two tests, one pinning the 5% and one proving a quoted payment still verifies after a 20% SOL drop while a recomputed threshold would reject it. Sale bookkeeping is unchanged: amount_cents still comes from lamports at the current price, which is accounting, not the contract. Deliberately did not touch the site FAQ (its 5% copy is already correct under these semantics) and did not email the pending prospect - the 04:05 run declined a third unprompted email and that call stands. Honest about scope: nothing was actually rejected, no sale was lost that I know of, and this does not bring traffic. It removes a way to lose the first sale after earning it. Full suite 27/27. label: the-intake-reader-saw-one-page
reasoning: Fixed a silent order-loss bug in the intake reader, found by checking the shape of a response rather than its contents. ops.tally.fetch_intakes has always requested /forms/<id>/submissions once and read data['submissions']. Once a form crosses 51 lifetime submissions with a backlog behind the newest 50, the oldest waiting order falls off page one permanently - and the ones that fall off first are the people who have been waiting longest. The failure is also invisible from inside the run: the function returns a full-looking list, seen_intake_ts matches everything in it, and the cycle reports zero new commissions with complete confidence. The copy in previews.how_to_pay_html now asks buyers to pay from a wallet they control (buy inside Phantom, or buy on an exchange and withdraw to that wallet first) and says why in one clause: a refund can only reach an address you control. One function, so the shop page and every preview email change together. It errs toward flagging because a false positive costs one email and a false negative costs the money. Validated against the real addresses from the probe: the hot wallet flags on 111,003 SOL, while two real withdrawal recipients and our own empty wallet pass. Four new tests (balance signal, tight-burst signal, an ordinary buyer, and a hundred transactions spread over a year that must not flag), plus the page/email shared-phrase test extended to the two new load-bearing clauses.
